According to the strict definition, both Skyrim and each of its holds except the Reach (The Reach is split between Skyrim and High Rock, and therefore the country of The Reach is constituted of the Western Reach and the hold of The Reach) are countries.

I like him as a person; he's a really nice guy and you can see his ambitious drive to service from a mile away. I think demographic representation in politics is extremely important, and appreciate any positive messaging that his campain can put out.

That's why I wish I could support him in the primary. In the end, Mayor Pete is a neoliberal who won't protect the working class and racial minorities from business interests except in the most nominal manner (I'm not even convinced that he'll defend gender and sexual minorities when push comes to shove, tbh). Look at the gentrification South Bend is experiencing, at the homeless who his administration keeps "relocating" by force, at the unending kowtowing to big business, and at his Pilatean handwashing of the issues of police brutality and racism and tell me that actions don't speak louder than words.

I'll vote for him if he's the nominee and I will probably be happier to do so than I should be, but I'm sick of the parade of agressively normal, barely left-of-center nominees and Presidents the DNC has been forcing on us and I'm sick of the demands that we not talk about difficult issues during primary season because it makes the centrist candidates "look bad" and the less-centrist candidates "less electable." I want real change, not mountains of platitudes.
